statement.excerpt: What I do know is that, across the board, a data center of anything above 50MW (or lower, in some cases) takes anywhere from 18 to 36 months to complete, and nobody has actually built a gigawatt data center despite how many people discuss them.
statement.document_title: Where Are All The Data Centers?

from_speaker: nobody has actually built a gigawatt data center
our_interpretation: Read 'across the board' as a general assertion covering completed data-center construction above 50 MW, rather than an average build time.

Count a delivered, energized construction phase exceeding 50 MW as completed data-center capacity even when further campus phases remain planned. This is an explicit interpretation of the unspecified unit of completion.
Measure construction through delivery and energization, rather than announcement of a future project. Do not require full customer utilization.
For the gigawatt clause, require at least 1 GW of completed, operational capacity at one site or campus; planned ultimate capacity and capacity spread across separate sites do not qualify.
Respect the surrounding text's explicit exception for the Colossus-1 conversion.
The observation concerns the historical record through publication. No starting date is supplied.
criteria.support_condition: A sufficiently comprehensive record supports the 18–36 month range for qualifying completed projects and establishes that no single site or campus had reached 1 GW of completed operational capacity by publication.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A documented qualifying completion outside 18–36 months contradicts the construction-time assertion. Alternatively, a verified site with at least 1 GW completed and operational by publication contradicts the gigawatt assertion.
